chapter: The Lunceford years: Europe, rivals and bandsmen
title: Gene Krupa's drumming and showmanship
summary: Crawford loved Krupa as a hard-hitting showman and good friend.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: What did you think of Krupa's drumming?
How did you like him as a swinger? Did you think he swung well?
Yeah, he lifted that band. Krupa was a livin' end. I loved that man. I knew him well. Hurt my heart when he passed. Yeah, I'm telling you.
Well, it -- what was it you liked about Krupa?

His playing. He had a lot of nerve. The man just could play. He had good hands, and he had -- and he was a good showman, sweating like mad, coat wringing wet. I didn't know how much he was making with Goodman, but you betcha Goodman was paying him more than I was paid. But that man loved to play. Can you cut it off? I want to ask you something.
